applies_why: The text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a single-verse row and states its grounds, which is exactly the act K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.
room: "is immediately qualified by": read one way, the judge only points to the chain answers in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4, so the verdict rests on that support and the rule is obeyed; read the other way, the judge makes the verse-unit's own two phrases -- "thy father" set against "my Father's business" -- the reason the row decides nothing, i.e., a verse admitting both readings used to ground UNDERDETERMINED; the second reading controls because the judge wrote no evaluation of the chain's support, and a verdict of UNDERDETERMINED rather than STANDS is accounted for only by the verse's internal two-sidedness.
why: The judge grounds the UNDERDETERMINED ruling on the single verse-unit's own counterbalancing phrases -- Mary's "thy father" qualified by the child's "my Father's business" -- letting a verse that admits both readings decide the row as undecided, which K-S2 forbids for either side.
